elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "The Company may terminate this Agreement for convenience, in whole or in part, upon ninety (90) days' written notice to HDI, effective on the date specified in that notice." This is an unconditional Customer election, i.e. a convenience right.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted Customer right requires ninety (90) days' written notice, not 30 days or fewer.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund mechanic anywhere in the rendered language; Section 4.2(a) only imposes a Termination Payment on the Company. To reach the preferred level the drafter would need express language that HDI refunds prepaid fees on a pro rata basis for the period after the effective date of termination.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Any termination by HDI under this Section 4.1 shall be effective only at the end of the then-current term." HDI therefore cannot exit effective mid-term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: "The Company may terminate this Agreement for convenience ... upon ninety (90) days' written notice to HDI, effective on the date specified in that notice" — 90 days sits at the top of the 60–90 day band, and the effective-date language removes the prior term-end/non-renewal-only reading.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Section 4.2(a) now ends "...divided by two, but in no event more than three (3) months of fees payable under Section 3." The cap is unconditional and applies to the only early-termination charge in the clause; the existing formula and instalment schedule are retained rather than expanded.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: "Any termination by HDI under this Section 4.1 shall be effective only at the end of the then-current term" expressly ties HDI's termination effective date to term end, which is what the auto-renewal sentence alone did not do; the retained "Such notice shall specify the date" sentence is now constrained by this limit rather than contradicting it.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Retained: "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other" — HDI's exit continues to require 90 days' notice; already met and correctly left untouched.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: an express 90-day Company convenience right effective on the date specified in its notice, HDI's termination effective only at the end of the then-current term, retention of HDI's existing 90-day notice obligation, and a three-months-of-Section-3-fees cap on the Termination Payment.

Preferred level fails on two elements: notice is 90 days rather than 30 or fewer, and there is no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund obligation on HDI. Do not infer a refund from the Termination Payment mechanic.

Minimal: two surgical operations (one inserted sentence pair in 4.1 and a cap tail in 4.2(a)); nothing favourable is deleted — the existing formula, the $800,000 deduction, the divide-by-two mechanic, the "if any" qualifier and the eight-instalment quarterly schedule all survive. "In whole or in part" tracks the rule's own model language and is not treated as an extra.

Preserves intent: the "Termination Date" definition still functions for the Section 4.2(a) formula, no cross-reference is left dangling, and the retained sentence requiring the notice to specify a termination date is narrowed (not contradicted) by the new HDI term-end limit.

Residual drafting risk to tighten, though not a failure: "three (3) months of fees payable under Section 3" is measurable only if Section 3 fees are periodic; if Section 3 is a variable revenue share, consider "three (3) months' average payments due under Section 3 over the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date" so the cap cannot be argued to be indeterminate.
Severity remains high because the unremediated clause left HDI with an effectively mid-term exit and the Company with an uncapped Net-Sales-based termination charge.
